sections.h2: Where is Cedar Rapids and how is the city divided?
sections.html:
Cedar Rapids is the county seat of Linn County, about 20 miles north of Iowa City and 128 miles northeast of Des Moines. It is the second most populous city in Iowa, with 137,710 residents in the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate of 137,935 for 2025.

The Cedar River splits the city into east and west sides, and 1st Avenue (U.S. Route 151 Business) splits it north from south. That makes four address quadrants. The city uses 14 ZIP codes, with downtown and Mays Island in 52401, so the first thing to confirm in any listing or offer is the exact quadrant and ZIP.

The city covers about 76 square miles at an elevation of 810 feet.

sections.h2: What is the history of Cedar Rapids?
sections.html:
Osgood Shepherd built the first cabin in 1837 or 1838, and the town was platted in 1841 as Rapids City. It was incorporated as Cedar Rapids on January 15, 1849, with fewer than 400 people.

Czech immigrants made up a large part of the early population: in 1856 about a quarter of roughly 1,600 residents were Czech. The first locomotive arrived on June 15, 1859. Sinclair meatpacking started in 1871 and the Quaker Oats mill was built in 1873. The county seat moved from Marion to Cedar Rapids in 1919.

Population passed 110,000 by 1970 and has grown slowly since, reaching 126,326 in 2010.

sections.h2: How did flooding and the 2020 derecho affect Cedar Rapids housing?
sections.html:
Cedar Rapids has two kinds of recent storm history that a seller needs to understand, river flooding and wind. Both left marks on the housing stock and on buyers' questions.

  • June 2008 flood: the Cedar River crested at a record 31.12 feet on June 13, against a previous record of 20 feet. Some 1,126 city blocks flooded, 7,749 properties were evacuated, including 5,900 homes, and at least 1,300 properties had to be demolished.
  • September 2016 flood: the river reached 22 feet on September 27, the second highest crest on record, with flood stage at 12 feet. More than 5,000 homes were affected. The city approved a $625 million, 20-year levee plan in 2015.
  • August 10, 2020 derecho: sustained winds of 60 to 80 mph and gusts of 110 mph or more hit the city. About 95 percent of Cedar Rapids lost power and 20 schools were damaged.

If a house sits in an area that took water or wind damage, expect a conventional buyer's inspection to look hard at the basement, roof and electrical system. A cash purchase can skip that repair negotiation.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in Cedar Rapids?
sections.html:
Collins Aerospace is the largest employer in Cedar Rapids, with between 5,000 and 9,999 employees according to the city's 2024 annual financial report as summarized on Wikipedia. Aegon USA keeps its U.S. headquarters in the city.

EmployerEmployees (2024 report range)
Collins Aerospace5,000 to 9,999
Aegon USA1,000 to 4,999
Cedar Rapids Community School District1,000 to 4,999
City of Cedar Rapids1,000 to 4,999

Grain processing is the largest sector, with about 4,000 direct jobs averaging $85,000 a year and about 8,000 indirect jobs. In February 2025, Quality Technology Services announced a $750 million data center expected to create about 30 jobs.

sections.h2: Which Cedar Rapids neighborhoods and school districts matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Cedar Rapids has twelve active neighborhood associations, and the ones nearest downtown include Wellington Heights, Oakhill Jackson and Moundview. Other named areas are Noelridge Park and Kenwood Park, plus informal districts such as Czech Village, New Bohemia (NewBo), Kingston Village and Wilderness Estates.

Four school districts serve parts of the city, and the address decides which one applies:

  • Cedar Rapids Community School District, with 15,589 students in 2023-24, 21 elementary schools, 6 middle schools and 5 high schools.
  • Linn-Mar Community School District, serving part of the northeast quadrant.
  • College Community School District, serving part of the southwest quadrant.
  • Marion Independent School District, serving a portion of the city.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and weather affect a Cedar Rapids house?
sections.html:
Interstate 380 runs north and south through the city as part of the Avenue of the Saints. U.S. 30, 151 and 218 and Iowa 13 and 100 also serve it, and the Eastern Iowa Airport is the regional airport. Four railroads run through town: Union Pacific, Crandic, Canadian National and Iowa Northern.

The climate is humid continental. Average precipitation is 35.91 inches a year and average snowfall is 26.7 inches, based on 1991 to 2020 normals at the airport. The record low is minus 30 degrees on January 31, 2019, and the record high is 110 degrees on July 6, 1911. Roofs, gutters and heating systems take real wear in that range.

sections.h2: What rental registration rules does Cedar Rapids have?
sections.html:
Cedar Rapids requires rental housing to hold a Certificate of Compliance before it can be legally occupied. The city issues it once the property meets the Housing Code and registration and inspection charges are paid.

Annual registration fees on the city's rental housing page are $50 for a single-family unit or condominium, $60 for a duplex, and $42 plus $13 per unit for a multi-family structure. A separate inspection fee schedule took effect July 1, 2023.

A landlord who is tired of managing a rental house can sell it with tenants in place or after they move out. Ask the buyer whether the registration will transfer or needs to be filed again.

sections.h2: What does Iowa require at a Cedar Rapids closing?
sections.html:
Every Iowa deed that moves through the Linn County Recorder carries a declaration of value, and most also carry a groundwater hazard statement. Iowa Code 558.69 sets out what the seller must report.

  • Wells, with approximate location and whether they meet state rules.
  • Private burial sites, underground storage tanks and known hazardous waste.
  • Solid waste disposal sites identified by the Department of Natural Resources.
  • Private sewage disposal systems, and whether they were inspected or are exempt at transfer.

At least one seller or the seller's agent signs it, and the buyer receives a copy. The owner is responsible for the accuracy of the answers. After the 2008 flood, owners of older properties should check records carefully for any tank or well that was removed, capped or replaced.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Cedar Rapids house work?
sections.html:
You can sell a Cedar Rapids house for cash without repairs, showings or a lender's appraisal. The steps are short.

  1. Send the address and a few details about the condition and any tenants.
  2. Receive a written offer based on the house as it stands.
  3. If the offer works, pick a closing date and let a title company prepare the deed, declaration of value and groundwater statement.
  4. Close, and record at the county.

Property taxes in Iowa turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1 for the two installments under Iowa Code 445.37, so ask the Linn County Treasurer what is paid before the closing date.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cedar Rapids?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 137,710 residents in Cedar Rapids, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 137,935. It is the second most populous city in Iowa.

faqs.q: How high did the Cedar River get in the 2008 flood?
faqs.a: The Cedar River crested at a record 31.12 feet on June 13, 2008. The earlier record was 20 feet, and 7,749 properties, including 5,900 homes, were evacuated.

faqs.q: Do landlords need a permit in Cedar Rapids?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental housing needs a Certificate of Compliance to be legally occupied, and registration fees are $50 a year for a single-family unit or condo, $60 for a duplex, and $42 plus $13 per unit for multi-family buildings.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Cedar Rapids house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Cedar Rapids Community Schools serves most of the city, while Linn-Mar, College Community and Marion Independent serve parts of it.

faqs.q: Who is the biggest employer in Cedar Rapids?
faqs.a: Collins Aerospace, with between 5,000 and 9,999 employees in the city's 2024 report, followed by Aegon USA, the school district and the city itself in the 1,000 to 4,999 range.
